gates.reason: Artifact writes use a predictable temporary pathname and follow any pre-existing symlink, allowing a local pathname attacker to overwrite another file.

Git tree output is parsed using newline splitting and trimming, so valid tracked Markdown filenames containing newlines or boundary whitespace can be omitted or changed, producing incomplete hygiene claims.

Inspected snapshot materialization, traversal, subprocess execution, normalization, and aggregation; the snapshot is reused across checks, traversal is iterative, and no release-gating hot-path regression was identified.

findings.title: Predictable artifact temporary path permits symlink overwrite
findings.what: writeDocHygieneArtifact constructs the temporary filename as `<output>.tmp-<pid>` and writes it without exclusive creation or a no-follow guarantee. If the output directory is writable by another local principal, that principal can pre-create this predictable path as a symlink; writeFileSync then follows it and overwrites the symlink target before renameSync replaces the link.
findings.fix: Create the temporary file atomically in the destination directory using an unpredictable name and exclusive/no-follow semantics, write through the secured file descriptor, then rename it; avoid a separate path-based chmod race by setting the final mode on that descriptor.
findings.acceptance: A test that pre-creates the formerly predictable temporary pathname as a symlink to a sentinel file must leave the sentinel unchanged, successfully publish the artifact through a separately and exclusively created temporary file, and leave the artifact mode at 0600.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 843-847 derive the name solely from the caller-controlled output path and process PID and call writeFileSync without `flag: "wx"` or no-follow protection; lines 909-912 also allow the destination to be selected with `--output`.

findings.title: Line-delimited Git parsing can omit valid Markdown filenames
findings.what: trackedMarkdownFiles invokes `git ls-tree -r --name-only` without `-z`, then splits on newlines and trims every pathname. Git permits filenames containing newlines and leading or trailing whitespace. Such paths are quoted/split or mutated by this parser and can fail the `.md` filter or be passed to Lychee under the wrong name. The detector can consequently report a clean or empty Markdown surface while committed Markdown was never checked.
findings.fix: Request NUL-delimited output with `git ls-tree -rz --name-only`, split on `\0`, discard only the final empty record, and preserve each pathname byte-for-byte without trim().
findings.acceptance: In a temporary Git repository containing tracked Markdown files with a newline and with leading/trailing whitespace in their names, trackedMarkdownFiles must return the exact names and the resulting hygiene run must scan them rather than report an empty or incomplete Markdown surface.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read lines 101-117 and confirmed both unsafe newline splitting and pathname trimming. Lines 627-637 then treat an empty parsed list as a completed score-10 check, making the missed-input claim reproducible rather than merely cosmetic.
